skill.description: Guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through building terminal user interfaces with OpenTUI core, React, or Solid.

I found no evidence of prompt injection, malicious intent, credential exfiltration, hidden network calls, or executable filesystem abuse in the reviewed documentation skill.

content.value_statement: Terminal interface work often requires framework-specific OpenTUI details across components, layout, input, animation, and testing. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structured references for building and troubleshooting OpenTUI apps.
actual_capabilities: Choose between OpenTUI core, React, and Solid based on project needs.
Guide component selection for text, containers, inputs, code display, diffs, and markdown.
Explain layout approaches using flexbox, absolute positioning, responsive sizing, and nested containers.
Provide keyboard, focus, paste, selection, and shortcut handling patterns.
Support animation, testing, snapshot, and troubleshooting workflows for OpenTUI apps.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples but does not install OpenTUI or run projects by itself.
Examples assume Bun and OpenTUI APIs match the referenced documentation version.
It cannot verify terminal rendering unless the user runs or tests the app.
It is focused on OpenTUI and is not a general terminal framework comparison skill.

use_cases.title: Start a new TUI app
use_cases.description: Select the right OpenTUI framework path and scaffold a first interface with components and layout.

use_cases.title: Add interactive terminal controls
use_cases.description: Implement inputs, focus handling, keyboard shortcuts, paste behavior, and escape or control key flows.

use_cases.title: Debug and test terminal rendering
use_cases.description: Use snapshots, test renderers, console overlays, and focused repro cases to fix OpenTUI issues.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a framework
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning a new OpenTUI app
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the opentui skill to help me choose between core, React, and Solid for a terminal app that needs [requirements]. Explain the tradeoffs and recommend one path.

prompt_templates.title: Build a component screen
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the opentui skill to design an OpenTUI screen with [components]. Include layout, focus behavior, and the relevant reference files to consult.

prompt_templates.title: Fix keyboard behavior
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the opentui skill to debug why [input or shortcut] is not working in my OpenTUI app. Check focus, key names, and framework-specific hook usage.

prompt_templates.title: Plan tests for a TUI feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the opentui skill to create a test plan for this OpenTUI feature: [feature]. Include snapshot tests, interaction tests, and debugging steps for failures.

output_examples.input: I need a React terminal app with a form and keyboard shortcuts.
output: Recommended React reconciler for familiar component patterns.
Use input components with explicit focus management.
Add keyboard hooks for escape and control shortcuts.
Test with the OpenTUI test renderer and snapshots.

output_examples.input: My OpenTUI logs do not appear while the app is running.
output: OpenTUI captures console output during rendering.
Use the console overlay, a keyboard toggle, or a temporary debug file.
Create a reproducible test instead of guessing at rendering bugs.

output_examples.input: I need a diff viewer in a terminal interface.
output: Use the code and diff component references.
Choose unified or split display based on available terminal width.
Plan scrolling and line-number behavior before styling.

best_practices: Start with the framework REFERENCE file, then read only the relevant API, configuration, pattern, or gotcha files.
Use renderer cleanup patterns instead of direct process termination when building interactive apps.
Write reproducible tests for layout, input, and rendering issues before changing several UI layers.
anti_patterns: Do not mix React and Solid component naming rules without checking the component reference.
Do not assume keyboard input works until the target input or delegated child has focus.
Do not rely on visible console output while an OpenTUI app is capturing terminal rendering.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build terminal user interfaces with OpenTUI core, React, or Solid.

faq.question: Does it support Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it choose a framework for me?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes decision trees for choosing core, React, or Solid based on requirements.

faq.question: Does it include testing guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers test renderer setup, snapshots, interaction testing, and debugging workflows.

faq.question: Can it run or verify my terminal app?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance, but execution and verification require local commands or tests.

faq.question: Is it only for new projects?
faq.answer: No. It also helps add components, fix input behavior, improve layouts, and troubleshoot existing apps.
